basis: The firm's own 1999 table lists Acacia as a 'Health services investment partnership', outcome 'Private partnership', and its 2008 to 2016 pages file Acacia Venture Partners under 'Investment Partnerships': an LP interest in another venture firm, not an operating company (D6, T5).

Control position (T3, D4): SHV's holding came from the May 1997 recapitalization in which 'Bain Capital, Inc., Sutter Hill Ventures and our senior management team collectively acquired securities representing approximately 88% of our outstanding voting power' (Therma-Wave S-1, 1999), buying the company from Toray and Shimadzu, which had owned it since fiscal 1992; Bain Capital Funds held 61% and SHV 18.1%. A majority recap by the firm's co-investor group is not a venture entry. The firm's 1999 table lists it as 'Private company', the post-recap holding.

note: Peptide drugs (abarelix), Waltham, Massachusetts (EDGAR registrant address; the 2000 S-1 still gave Cambridge). GlaxoSmithKline bought it in early 2007 (Praecis deregistered on 2007-02-16), so acquired, below_1b; agrees with the Greylock row. The firm's 1999 table: 'Private company'. Entry: the 2000 S-1 shows Series A convertible preferred ($10.5M liquidation preference) as the first financing of a company that began operations in January 1994, and G. Leonard Baker of SHV on the board since March 1994; SHV's 1.29M common-equivalent shares far exceed its only later purchase in the S-1's table (84,409 Series E shares), so the entry reads as the Series A, dated to Baker's arrival (medium).

Removable-disk backup and archive (RDX, InfiniVault), Boulder, Colorado. In 2011 it sold its RDX business to Tandberg Data (May) and InfiniVault to Imation (August) and wound down (ProStor's own release, https://www.rdxworks.com/prostor-sells-rdx-technology-tandberg.aspx; eWeek, 'Imation Acquires InfiniVault From ProStor Systems'): an asset sale out of a wind-down, so acquired, below_1b. DISPUTE of the Seed band: the band read the June 2010 $5.5M Form D, but that filing says ProStor was incorporated over five years before (the firm's page: founded May 2004), and its director Ron Bernal had left SHV (Sequel from 2006, NEA from 2010; D5), so the filing dates neither the company's first round nor SHV's entry (the PRO-157 withholding rule). SHV's round is not on record. No Seed entry, so no graduation.

All-flash storage, incorporated October 2009 as OS76, Inc. inside SHV's office (Wikipedia; the S-1), now named Everpure, headquartered in Santa Clara. DISPUTE of the Pre-Seed band (D3): the band read the $3,050 founders' filing of October 2009 (Mike Speiser and John Colgrove filing from Palo Alto); the round SHV's fund bought is the first preferred round, which the 2015 S-1 names Series A ($5.075M; the $5M Form D of 2009-11-04), with Speiser as SHV's board designee. Valuation: market cap $43.12B on 2026-09-28 (stockanalysis.com, ticker P), replacing the prefilled 2025 public float of $17.0B, which is corroboration only; 10b_plus either way, agreeing with the Greylock, IVP and Redpoint rows.

Performance marketing (online lead generation), Foster City. Entry: the 2009 S-1 says 'The holders of a majority of our Series A preferred stock ... have designated Gregory Sands and James Simons' for the board, the investor rights agreement gives one of those seats to a nominee of Sutter Hill Ventures, and Sands (SHV since 1998) has been a director since July 1999, three months after the April 1999 incorporation: SHV bought the Series A. Public (Nasdaq QNST), below_1b as prefilled (market cap $811M on 2026-09-28). Not a Seed entry, so no graduation.

Network security posture and exposure management, founded 2004 as RedSeal Systems. STG Partners made an equity investment in April 2019 (FinSMEs) and the company still trades under its own name (product launches through August 2025); its contact page gives 'RedSeal, Inc. c/o Symphony Technology Group, 1300 El Camino Real, Menlo Park' as headquarters. Whether STG holds control is not on record, so private; no priced round at $1B or more found, below_1b. DISPUTE of the Pre-Seed band: it read a $2,088 option filing of December 2010; the first e-filed round was the $12M equity round of September 2009, whose Form D says the company was incorporated over five years before, and SHV listed it from 2008 with Tench Coxe as its director. SHV's entry round is not on record.

funding_rounds.round: Form D, equity, round not named

note: Robotic hair restoration (ARTAS), San Jose (the later Form Ds). Merged with Venus Concept in November 2019, the combined company taking the Venus Concept name: acquired as prefilled, below_1b. Entry: the 2017 S-1's voting agreement gives Sutter Hill Ventures the right to elect 'the other Series A designee' (Alloy Ventures the first), and Jeffrey Bird of SHV has been a director since July 2005; the Series A ($11.3M liquidation preference) was the first preferred round of a company incorporated in November 2002, so SHV entered at the Series A, dated to Bird's arrival. SHV also bought 4,450,948 Series C shares from 2014. The June 2011 Form D the prefill dated from was a later round. No Seed entry, so no graduation.

Email deliverability and certification data, New York. Validity bought it in May 2019 (MediaPost, 'Email Vendor Return Path Being Sold To Validity'), so acquired, below_1b; agrees with the USV row. DISPUTE of the Seed band: Return Path dates from 1999 (Flatiron invested in its first venture round that year) and USV's own post of 2008-10-30 (https://www.usv.com/writing/2008/10/return-path/) names 'our good friends Sutter Hill' as an existing investor when USV made a later-stage investment, so the July 2009 $5.5M Form D (Greg Sands of SHV a director; the filing says incorporated over five years before) is neither the company's first round nor SHV's entry. SHV's round is not on record. No Seed entry, so no graduation.

3D product-graphics and visualization software. SAP agreed to buy it on 2011-09-06, describing it as 'based in San Ramon, California, and Auckland, New Zealand' (SAP's release, https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/sap-to-acquire-3-d-visualization-software-maker-right-hemisphere-129333453.html), so acquired, below_1b; US and San Ramon agree with Sequoia's row (the 2009 Form D gave Pleasanton). DISPUTE of the Series A band: the March 2009 $10M Form D the band read says the company was incorporated over five years before, and SHV already listed it in 2008 (Jim White of SHV its director), so that filing does not date SHV's entry. SHV's round is not on record.

Hotel search (metasearch) site, Mountain View (the Form Ds). Lola, Paul English's travel-agent app, acquired Room 77 in November 2016 (Lola's own post, https://medium.com/@lola.com/lola-to-acquire-hotel-search-site-room-77-55f9404cf675; PhocusWire, 'Travel startup Lola acquires Room 77, the hotel metasearch platform'; Skift, 'Lola Travel Agent App Acquires Room 77 Technology') and kept it running as a hotel search tool, so the business continued under a buyer: acquired, below_1b. This disputes the Felicis and General Catalyst rows (defunct) with cited evidence; Felicis's own note records the Lola deal. The prefilled Growth entry (the $30.3M round from December 2012, James White of SHV a director) stands.

Customer loyalty and Net Promoter software, San Mateo (the Form Ds). NICE bought it: it trades as NICE Satmetrix by June 2018 (PR Newswire, 'Kaiser Permanente Again Tops Annual Consumer Loyalty Study'; CX Today, https://cxtoday.com/nice-satmetrix-review-insights-into-voc-from-nice), so acquired, below_1b. DISPUTE of the Seed band: the September 2009 filing it read is a $1.0M debt offering (bridge notes) by a company its own Form D says was incorporated over five years before, followed by equity rounds of $4.5M (2010) and $16.8M (2011); a note is not a seed round. SHV's entry round is not on record (Jim White of SHV a director from the first e-filing). No Seed entry, so no graduation.

note: SeeSaw Networks, media planning and buying for out-of-home digital video networks, San Francisco (100 Bush Street; the Form Ds), incorporated 2005. Its filings end with 2011 bridge notes, its domain seesawnetworks.com is now for sale, and data vendors list it as closed with no acquirer; no buyer was found, so defunct (a quiet shutdown; no dated notice), below_1b. Entry: the first e-filed Form Ds (2009) are convertible notes with Jim Gaither and Tench Coxe of SHV as directors; vendors date a first round to November 2006 with SHV as its main institutional investor, but no citable source names SHV's round, so undetermined. NAME COLLISION: First Round Capital's 'seesaw' row is Seesaw the classroom learning journal, a different company; do not align.

funding_rounds.round: Form D, equity, round not named

note: Photo books, cards and prints, now headquartered in San Jose (Wikipedia); IPO 2006, taken private by Apollo in 2019: acquired as prefilled, below_1b. DISPUTE of the band's date: the 2006 S-1 says 'In November 2005, we sold 1,353,730 shares of our Series F preferred stock to Sutter Hill Ventures and affiliated persons and entities at a purchase price of $14.774 per share' (about $20.0M), with a voting agreement giving SHV a board seat (James White); SHV also bought common from former officers in 2005 and 2006. The entry is that Series F, Growth; the 2011 $222M Form D the prefill used was stock issued for the Tiny Prints acquisition, not a financing SHV joined.

RISC-V processor IP and chips, Santa Clara (agrees with the Coatue and Spark rows). Private; the Series G of 2026-04-09 ($400M, led by Atreides, NVIDIA and Apollo joining) valued it at $3.65B (The Next Web), 1b_plus, matching both siblings. DISPUTE of the Seed band: Wikipedia records that 'In September 2015, SiFive raised $5 million in Series A funding', the company's first round (Form D, first sale 2015-09-04, $5.06M), and LinuxGizmos (2017-05-08) reports the $8.5M Series B 'led by Spark Capital, and also included participation from Osage University Partners and earlier investor Sutter Hill Ventures', bringing the total to $13.5M: the only earlier money was that $5M Series A, so SHV's entry is the Series A. Stefan Dyckerhoff of SHV is director and executive officer on the Form Ds. SHV later co-led the 2019 Series D. No Seed entry, so no graduation.

Silicon anode battery materials, Alameda ('headquartered in Alameda, California', its 2018 release). Valuation: GeekWire (2026-07-21) reports that Sila 'was valued at close to $2 billion two years ago', the June 2024 Series G that SHV led (Bloomberg, 2024-09-24: 'Sila Nanotechnologies Takes $1 Billion Valuation Haircut With Latest Round', down from the January 2021 Series F mark); the July 2026 $300M round disclosed no valuation. So 1b_plus at about $2.0B, stale (older than 24 months). This disputes the 8VC row (below_1b on an assumed repricing, with no figure) with a cited priced mark. DISPUTE of the Growth band: the band dated SHV's entry to the 2018 Series D, but the firm listed Sila under Mike Speiser in 2013 (a Common Crawl capture of shv.com/portfolio of December 2013, and the 2013 Wayback page), so SHV held it about five years before that round; the 2018 release calls SHV the Series D lead and names no earlier SHV round, so the round SHV first entered is not on record.

Rail ticket distribution and booking technology, founded 2009 near Boston. Expedia bought a majority stake in 2017 (Skift, 'Expedia Spent $148 Million to Buy SilverRail'), and management bought the business back from Expedia Group in October 2020 (PhocusWire, 'SilverRail Technologies in management buyout from Expedia Group'); SilverRail then raised again as an independent issuer (Form D, first sale 2023-02-27, $15M of $20M sold) from 27 Maiden Lane, London. So it is private today: fresher cited evidence than Accel's row (acquired, Expedia), which should align. No priced round at $1B found, below_1b. Country and city follow the 2023 Form D (London, United Kingdom), disputing the Woburn-era US prefill. The prefilled Series A entry (the 2009 round, James White of SHV a director) stands.

funding_rounds.round: Form D, equity, round not named

note: Secure hyperconverged infrastructure (SkySecure), Mountain View. Fortune (2016-03-15, https://fortune.com/2016/03/15/gv-cisco-fund-skyport-systems/): Stefan Dyckerhoff of SHV 'originally incubated the company at his venture capital firm while serving as interim CEO', and SHV was an existing investor in the $30M Series C led by GV. Cisco bought it in early 2018, so acquired, below_1b. DISPUTE of the Seed band (D3): the incubation's first preferred round, which its own Form D names 'Series A Preferred Stock' ($7.0M, first sale 2013-06-28), is SHV's entry, not the Seed the band read from its size. No Seed entry, so no graduation.

Work management software, Bellevue, Washington. IPO 2018, taken private by Blackstone and Vista in January 2025 (Wikipedia): acquired as prefilled, so below_1b with no figure; agrees with the Insight row. The prefilled Growth entry (the $35M round of 2014, Jim White of SHV a director) stands.

Cloud data platform. HQ: the FY2026 10-K (filed 2026-03-20) gives principal executive offices at 135 Constitution Drive, Menlo Park (Snowflake moved back from Bozeman), fresher than the Bozeman on the Coatue, General Catalyst and Sequoia rows. Valuation: market cap $115.65B on 2026-09-28 (stockanalysis.com), 100b_plus, replacing the prefilled 2025 public float ($73.5B, 10b_plus), which disagreed with all three siblings. DISPUTE of the Pre-Seed band (D3): Crunchbase News (2020-10-14): 'Sutter Hill led Snowflake's $5 million Series A in August 2012, and Managing Director Mike Speiser served as the company's founding CEO'; Business Insider (2020-09-21) likewise; the S-1 has Speiser's seat 'elected by the holders of a majority of our Series A convertible preferred stock ... as the designee of Sutter Hill Ventures'. The Series A Form D gives first sale 2013-03-08 ($5.0M at about $0.35). Open point: the S-1 and a retroactive Form D also show a Series Seed ($0.9M at $0.1719, first sale 2012-08-24, while Speiser was CEO) whose buyer the record does not name; if SHV's fund bought it, the entry is that Seed and the named Series A of March 2013 graduates it.

Cloud log management and analytics, Redwood City. IPO 2020, taken private by Francisco Partners in May 2023 for $1.7B (Wikipedia): acquired as prefilled, below_1b. Entry: Crunchbase News (2020-10-14): 'Sutter Hill began investing in Sumo Logic around the time of its $15 million Series B round in January 2012', which fits the firm's 2012 listing; Growth, as the band read, but dated 2012-01 instead of the band's 2015 Form D.

Small-business lending (Swift Capital), Wilmington, Delaware (the Form Ds). PayPal bought it in August 2017 (The News Journal, https://www.delawareonline.com/story/money/business/2017/08/11/paypal-buys-wilmington-startup/559768001/), so acquired, below_1b. Entry: the first e-filed Form D (a 2010 amendment of a 2009 paper filing) covers 'Series A1 and Series A1-1 Preferred Stock' sold from 2009-02-04 ($6.24M), with Tench Coxe of SHV a director; the company was incorporated in 2006 and the A1 name implies an earlier Series A, so the round SHV entered is not on record (the band was withheld). Later: Series A2 (2011, $12.8M of $15M sold), secured notes (2012), equity (2014).

funding_rounds.round: Series A1 and Series A1-1 preferred

note: Network intelligence and monitoring, San Francisco. Cisco completed its purchase on 2020-08-07 (Cisco newsroom, https://newsroom.cisco.com/c/r/newsroom/en/us/a/y2020/m08/cisco-completes-acquisition-of-thousand-eyes.html), so acquired, below_1b; agrees with Sequoia's row. Entry: Wikipedia: 'In 2014, Sutter Hill Ventures led a Series B round, joined by Sequoia Capital and Salesforce.com, to invest $20M' after Sequoia's 2011 Series A; the $20M Form D gives first sale 2014-03-07 with Stefan Dyckerhoff of SHV a director. Series B reads Growth; not a Seed entry, so no graduation.

Cancer drugs (evofosfamide), South San Francisco; merged with Molecular Templates in 2017 (the prefill's acquired), below_1b. DISPUTE of the Growth band: the band read a $35M 2009 private placement, made after the 2005 IPO. The 2004 S-1 lists entities affiliated with Sutter Hill Ventures among the Series A buyers (1,589,079 shares) and the Series B buyers (2,140,175 shares). The Series A ($9M at $1.00 after a reverse split) closed from October 2001 to 2002-08-15; SHV's stake exceeds everything sold before the August 2002 close (750,000 shares), so the entry is the Series A, dated to that close.

Cloud field-service management software (ETAdirect), Beachwood, Ohio (the Form Ds). Oracle bought it in 2014: acquired as prefilled, below_1b. The prefilled Series A entry (the $17.2M round of April 2011, Andy Sheehan of SHV a director) stands.

Fiber backhaul for wireless carriers, St. Petersburg, Florida (the firm's own page and the Form Ds). CS&L, now Uniti, completed its purchase in 2016 (Telecom Ramblings, https://www.telecomramblings.com/2016/09/csl-completes-tower-cloud-buy-launches-uniti/), so acquired, below_1b. The prefilled Growth entry (the $74M round of September 2009, Tench Coxe of SHV a director) stands.

Data security and rights management, Palo Alto (the Form Ds). HelpSystems (now Fortra) bought it in 2020 (Wikipedia), so acquired, below_1b. DISPUTE of the Series A band: Wikipedia records the $14M Series A of November 2014 (its Form D lists only the CEO) and 'In February 2016, Vera announced a $17 million Series B round, led by Sutter Hill Ventures', and Stefan Dyckerhoff of SHV first appears on the $21.8M Form D filed in March 2016 (first sale given as 2015-03-10). SHV entered at the Series B: Growth.

Non-invasive prenatal testing, Redwood City (the 2011 and 2012 Form Ds). Illumina bought it in January 2013 (GEN, https://www.genengnews.com/news/illumina-acquires-verinata-health/), so acquired, below_1b. The prefilled Series A entry (the $10M round of October 2009, Jeff Bird of SHV a director) stands.

Video indexing and cataloging software (VideoLogger), San Mateo, California (177 Bovet Road; its 2000 S-1 and EDGAR record); Autonomy bought it in 2003 (its last EDGAR filings), so acquired, below_1b. DISPUTE of the prefilled country RU, a wrong Wikidata join on a one-word name: the company was US. Entry: the 2000 S-1 shows Series A preferred (about 4.1M shares at roughly $0.75, most outstanding by March 1996) as the first financing after the March 1995 Delaware reincorporation, and William Younger of SHV a director since April 1995; the S-1's recent-sales table shows SHV buying Series B to E, yet SHV and its affiliates held 3.18M shares against 1.61M bought in B to E, so the rest predates 1997: the entry reads as the Series A (medium).

Cathepsin and protease inhibitors, Menlo Park (the Form Ds and the 2014 S-1). It withdrew its $50M IPO in October 2014 (Renaissance Capital, 'TPG-backed biotech Virobay withdraws $50 million IPO'); no later financing, filing, deal or shutdown notice was found (a vendor profile calls it inactive, which is not a citable fate), so unknown, below_1b. Entry: the S-1 says the company 'issued 30,500,001 shares of Series A Stock from 2006 through December 31, 2008' at $1.00, and Jeffrey Bird of SHV has been a director since August 2006, three months after the May 2006 incorporation, together with TPG's director: SHV entered at the Series A. SHV also bought $2M of the Series B.

Business-process integration middleware (BusinessWare), Sunnyvale (EDGAR registrant address; Mountain View at its 1999 IPO). Its founders' company took it private in 2007 (Vitria deregistered on 2007-03-19), so acquired, below_1b. The firm's 1999 table: 'Public company'. Entry: the 1999 S-1's table of preferred purchases shows Sutter Hill Ventures (like Brentwood) buying no Series A or A1 and 2,481,327 shares of the Series B sold in October 1997 at $1.81, then Series C and D; William Younger of SHV a director since 1997. Series B reads Growth.

Online advertising for small businesses, Irvine (the Form D). TechCrunch (2011-12-28, https://techcrunch.com/2011/12/28/bank-shuts-down-local-online-advertising-company-webvisible-for-not-paying-debts/): Silicon Valley Bank foreclosed on its loan and took the assets, with no buyer for the business: defunct, below_1b; agrees with Redpoint's row. Funded by SHV, Redpoint and Adams Street (over $17M per TechCrunch). The only e-filed Form D (February 2010, $20M, James White of SHV a director from the firm's address) is not the first round of a company founded in 2001, and the round SHV entered is not on record.

funding_rounds.round: Form D, equity, round not named

note: Small-molecule immuno-oncology drug discovery, Waltham, Massachusetts (100 Beaver Street; the Form Ds). Its last filing is a 2018 Form D ($1.0M of $1.5M sold), its domain no longer resolves, and data vendors list it as closed; no acquirer or later round was found, so defunct (a quiet wind-down, not a dated notice), below_1b. The prefilled Seed entry (the $6.0M first round of December 2015, Jeff Bird of SHV a director) stands; the 2018 $1M raise is not a later priced round at twice the entry. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Electronic brachytherapy (miniature x-ray source), Sunnyvale (the Form Ds). iCAD bought it at the end of 2010 and sold the Xoft business to Elekta in 2023 (DOTmed, https://www.dotmed.com/news/story/61531), so acquired, below_1b. DISPUTE of the Series A band: the June 2009 filing it read is a debt offering (notes with warrants) by a company its own Form D says was incorporated over five years before (the firm's page: established 1998), and SHV listed it from 2008. SHV's entry round is not on record.

Brand knowledge and listings software, New York. Public (NYSE YEXT), below_1b as prefilled (market cap $636M on 2026-09-28, agreeing with the Insight and IVP rows). DISPUTE of the Growth band (it read a 2014 $50M Form D): the 2017 S-1's preferred stock table gives the Series A an issue date of May 2008 ($0.317 a share, $1.82M), and Andrew Sheehan of SHV has been a director since May 2008; SHV was listed from 2010 and also bought Series F. The entry reads as the Series A, dated to Sheehan's arrival (medium). Not a Seed entry, so no graduation.

Online video (Youku, merged with Tudou in 2012), Beijing. Alibaba bought it (agreed November 2015, closed 2016), so acquired, below_1b. Entry: the 2010 F-1 says the Series A of November 2005 went to Chengwei and Farallon, and 'The investors in our Series B1 and B2 preferred share private placements included Chengwei Funds, Farallon Funds and certain Sutter Hill Funds'; the B1 was issued in January 2007, and SHV holds B1, B2, C, D and E but no A. Series B reads Growth. G. Leonard Baker of SHV a director since 2007.

AAC Technologies, miniature acoustic, haptic and optical components for phones, listed in Hong Kong (2018.HK) since August 2005; 'founded in 1993 and is headquartered in Shenzhen' (stockanalysis profile; Cayman-registered). Market cap HKD 45.04B on 2026-09-28 (stockanalysis), HKD 45.04B @ ECB 2026-09-28 (HKD/EUR 8.9258, EUR/USD 1.1378) = $5.74B, 1b_plus. The firm listed 'AAC' on its networking pages in captures from 2010 to 2016; a vendor profile names SHV an institutional investor, but no source dates SHV's entry or names a round, so undetermined. Worth a check: if SHV bought after the 2005 listing, the position is a post-IPO purchase and the row leaves under T3.

TGF-beta superfamily biopharmaceuticals (luspatercept, sotatercept), Cambridge, Massachusetts. Merck bought it in November 2021: acquired as prefilled, below_1b. SHV signed Acceleron's amended investor rights and co-sale agreements of 2011-12-22 (the Series F financing) as an existing preferred holder (the 2013 DRS exhibits) and listed the company from 2008; the 2013 S-1 names SHV neither as a 5% holder nor as a buyer of any series, so the round SHV entered is not on record.

Formerly FaceTime Communications (the firm's 1999 table: 'FaceTime Communications, Web customer interaction, Private company'): security and compliance for instant messaging, unified communications and social media, Redwood City (Wikipedia). K1 Investment Management bought it in November 2017 and combined it with Smarsh (Law.com, https://www.law.com/legaltechnews/2017/11/15/k1-investments-to-merge-smarsh-and-actiance/), so acquired, below_1b. SHV held it by 1999 (Tench Coxe its director); the round SHV entered is not on record.

Video game publisher, founded 1 October 1979, Santa Monica. Wikipedia: Jim Levy 'helped the four to secure about $1 million in capital from Sutter Hill Ventures' at the founding; the firm's 1999 table: 'Entertainment software, Public company'. Activision merged with Vivendi Games in 2008 to form Activision Blizzard, which Microsoft bought in October 2023, so acquired, below_1b. The record does not name the founding round, so the stage is undetermined (the entry itself dates to 1979).

Supply-chain planning software, Los Angeles (its 2000 S-1). The 2000 IPO was withdrawn and FreeMarkets' 2001 agreement to buy it did not close; Adexa stayed independent until Eyelit Technologies bought it in January 2025 (Business Wire, 'Eyelit Technologies Acquires Adexa to Expand Smart Factory and Supply Chain Solutions'; adexa.com now redirects to eyelit.com), so acquired, below_1b. Entry: the S-1 says Adexa sold 4,130,170 Series A shares at $1.18 from 1997-08-04 to February 1998, of which entities associated with Sutter Hill Ventures bought 3,160,750 (all but 55,000 shares were issued in 1997); William Younger of SHV a director from January 1998. SHV also bought Series B (1998) and C (2000).

Service-delivery and network API software for telecom operators, Belfast (Silicon Republic: 'Belfast tech firm Aepona'). Intel bought it in April 2013 (Amadeus Capital, its largest investor: 'Amadeus' Aepona Acquired by Intel'), so acquired, below_1b. Amadeus's release names Irish and French venture investors, BlackBerry Partners and SAP but not SHV; the firm listed Aepona in 2010 and 2012 and no source names the round SHV joined.

AIDA Corp., computer-aided engineering tools for large system designers, 'based in Santa Clara, Calif.' (UPI, 1987-11-03, https://www.upi.com/Archives/1987/11/03/Teradyne-to-acquire-AIDA-Corp/1450562914000/): Teradyne agreed to buy it for about 1.8M Teradyne shares, and the firm's 1999 table says 'Acquired by Teradyne', so acquired, below_1b. DISPUTE of the prefilled country AT, a wrong Wikidata join on a one-word name. Focus follows the EDA precedent in this book (Avant!, Mentor Graphics). SHV's round is not on record.

Thrombocytopenia drugs (AKR-501, later avatrombopag, Doptelet). Eisai completed its purchase of AkaRx, 'Headquarters: Bridgewater, New Jersey', on 2010-01-06 for about $255 million (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/eisai-completes-acquisition-of-akarx-inc-and-continues-development-of-akr-501-for-thrombocytopenia-80845092.html), exercising the option it gained with MGI Pharma; acquired, below_1b. SHV listed it from 2008 to 2016; the round SHV entered is not on record.

Small-business information and media site, San Francisco, co-founded 1999 by Richard Harroch. NBCi bought the first company in March 2000; after that entity was broken up in 2002 Harroch bought back the core assets, raised a Series B (July 2004, $10M) and a Series C (February 2006, $12.4M), and Dun & Bradstreet bought AllBusiness for $55M in December 2007 (Wikipedia: AllBusiness.com), so acquired, below_1b. SHV listed it from 2010; which round it bought is not on record.
